class.name: NetwClockHandle
class.brief_description: The network clock of one session, gathered onto one object.
class.description: A client over the [code]clock_*[/code] family on [NetwMultiplayer], reached as [method Netw.clock] from any [Node]. Every member forwards to a flat verb, and the flat verb is the stable spelling: this repository's own suites, examples and test kit call [NetwMultiplayer] directly, and a game reaches for this when it would rather hold the clock as one object. [codeblock] var c := Netw.clock(self) c.before_tick.connect(sample_input) c.on_tick.connect(step) label.text = "tick %d" % c.tick [/codeblock] [b]What this object buys over the flat surface is its two signals.[/b] [Netw] is static and a static class publishes none, so a component that drives itself off the tick has to name the session to hear it. One handle exists per session for the life of that session, because a session has exactly one clock, so there is nothing to select and nothing to pass: the door is the clock. [method Netw.configure_clock] is the other half of the pair. That verb DECLARES, before the session comes up, and answers a [NetwClockConfig] to author. This one REACHES, once it is running. A param this object refuses to set is a param the declaration owns: [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_TICKRATE] answers [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED] here, because a session cannot change its tickrate underneath the peers already synchronized to it.

method.name: monitor
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_get_monitor]: the live reading named by [param monitor], one of [enum NetwMultiplayer.ClockMonitor]. Answers [code]0.0[/code] for a clock that has measured nothing yet.

method.name: param
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_get_param]: the setting named by [param param], one of [enum NetwMultiplayer.ClockParam].

method.name: set_param
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_set_param]. Writes the setting named by [param param] at runtime, answering [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED] for a param the declaration owns rather than silently keeping the old value. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK written ┠╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED param is a param the declaration owns, such as the tickrate ┠╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER param names no ClockParam value ┖╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED this handle's session is gone [/codeblock]

members.member: How many times this peer's simulation has fallen behind the clock and had to catch up. [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_get_simulation_behind_count].
Whether a [NetwClockConfig] has settled on this session, which is what [method Netw.configure_clock] declares. A component that steps on the tick reads this before it trusts [member tick].

Whether this peer's clock has agreed a tick with server authority. A server reads [code]true[/code] because it is the authority; a client reads [code]false[/code] until the first sync lands. [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_is_synchronized].
The current network tick, the number every [NetwRecord] and every lag-compensation query is stamped against. [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_get_tick].

signal.name: before_tick
signal.description: Emitted before the simulation steps [param tick], carrying that step's [param delta]. This is where input for the tick is sampled, because what is written here is what the tick then simulates. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.clock_before_tick].

signal.name: on_tick
signal.description: Emitted as the simulation steps [param tick], carrying that step's [param delta]. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.clock_on_tick].
